event: UFC Fight Night 293 - Cortes-Acosta vs. Walker

johnny-walker-waldo-cortes-acosta.summary: On nine days' notice, Walker circled and chopped Cortes-Acosta's lead leg with low kicks from the opening bell, while the much heavier man pinned him on the fence, put him down briefly and kneed him in the clinch; Sherdog's three scorers gave Walker round 1 on the kicks. Both were tired in round 2, and Cortes-Acosta took it with right hands and by finishing the round on top after Walker went down. Early in round 3 an overhand right wobbled Walker, but off a separation he landed a question-mark kick and a backfist, then dropped Cortes-Acosta with a right hand and finished him at 2:27, the first stoppage loss of Cortes-Acosta's career.
johnny-walker-waldo-cortes-acosta.turning_point: Round 3: Walker's question-mark kick and backfist off Herzog's break, a minute after he had been wobbled himself.

checks.claim: Walker gets knocked out when opponents press; the bigger, never-stopped Cortes-Acosta weathers R1 and walks him down: KO/TKO, R2
checks.note: Cortes-Acosta pressed, won round 2 and wobbled Walker in round 3, but Walker stayed up and stopped him.
Took clean right hands in rounds 2 and 3, was wobbled once, and was never in real danger of going.

tatiana-suarez-virna-jandiroba.summary: Suarez went for single legs from the first exchange, but Jandiroba stayed upright on the fence, landing knees and elbows while hopping on one leg, and caught her with the cleaner right hands early in round 2. Suarez's top time came late in round 2, when she sprawled on a Jandiroba shot, and in round 3 off a takedown against the fence; she controlled from half guard with short elbows and got out of kneebars at the end of both rounds. Suarez won 30-27, 30-27, 29-28; all three Sherdog scorers had it 30-27.
tatiana-suarez-virna-jandiroba.turning_point: Late in round 2: Suarez's sprawl on Jandiroba's takedown attempt put her on top for the first time.

checks.claim: Suarez's wrestling against a grappler who has mostly been the one shooting; Jandiroba's guard keeps it on the cards: decision
checks.note: Won the fight from top position in rounds 2 and 3; Jandiroba's guard stopped any finish.

checks.note: Jandiroba stuffed nearly every single leg for seven minutes; Suarez got top position off a sprawl and one late takedown, and that won the rounds.

elijah-smith-davey-grant.summary: Grant came forward with low kicks and they traded right hands, until Smith answered a left hand with a power shot that staggered Grant backward. Smith followed him and knocked him unconscious with a final right hand on the way down at 1:00 of round 1, the first knockout loss of Grant's 27-fight career. It earned Smith a $100,000 bonus.

checks.claim: Grant has never been knocked out but has been submitted five times, so a Smith finish is a choke, after Grant's volume takes R1: submission, R2
checks.note: Smith knocked Grant out in 60 seconds.

lucas-fernando-billy-elekana.summary: Fernando out-worked Elekana for two rounds with the jab, kicks to every level and knees and hooks to the body in the clinch, hurting him with a right hand and a knee in round 1 and turning him onto the fence every time Elekana went for the body lock. A tiring Fernando gave up a trip takedown in round 3 and spent most of it in closed guard, where Elekana won the round with elbows but did little damage. Fernando won 29-28 on all three cards and all three of Sherdog's.

checks.claim: Override: Fernando's kicks to every level break down Elekana, who was hurt by body work before: KO/TKO, R2
checks.note: The body work hurt and slowed Elekana and won the first two rounds, but there was no stoppage and Fernando faded in round 3.

nina-nikolija-milosevic-priscila-cachoei.summary: Milosevic crashed in behind a jumping kick, took Cachoeira down in the first seconds and jumped to her back, then punched her from the back and mount for the rest of round 1, with a look at an arm-triangle; two of Sherdog's scorers had it 10-8. Cachoeira swung back early in round 2 and landed a combination, but Milosevic took her down again, went to mount and the back and finished her with elbows and punches at 3:40.

checks.claim: Cachoeira has been submitted five times after being dropped or taken down; Milosevic finishes early: submission, R1
checks.note: Taken down and on her back at once, as expected, but finished by ground strikes in round 2, not a choke.

mitch-raposo-marcos-degli.summary: The debuting Degli won round 1 on the counter, staggering Raposo with a left hook and landing an elbow, and all three Sherdog scorers gave it to him. From round 2 Raposo took the center and out-threw him with one-twos, leg kicks and body shots while Degli waited; in round 3 an elbow opened a cut on Raposo's head, but he kept up the volume, hurt Degli to the body and reversed his late takedown attempt. Raposo won 29-28 on all three cards, ending Degli's 13-fight streak.
mitch-raposo-marcos-degli.turning_point: Round 2: Degli stopped throwing and Raposo took the center for good.

checks.claim: Degli's finishing streak beats Raposo, who goes the distance and gets back up: decision
checks.note: It went to the cards as picked, but Raposo won the last two rounds on every card.
Sharp in round 1, then quiet: out-thrown in rounds 2 and 3 by a UFC veteran.

oliver-schmid-keiichiro-nakamura.summary: Schmid out-boxed Nakamura for two rounds, answering his inside leg kicks with cleaner combinations, left hooks and spinning kicks to the body, and won both on every Sherdog card; a low blow paused round 2. Nakamura came on in round 3 and floored Schmid with a left hook, nearly finishing him with punches, but Schmid got up, caught a kick for a takedown and saw out the round. Schmid won 29-28 on all three cards.
oliver-schmid-keiichiro-nakamura.turning_point: Round 3: Nakamura's knockdown, and Schmid's takedown off a caught kick that bought him time.

checks.claim: Nakamura gives away early exchanges and grows into fights; Schmid's losses came late: KO/TKO, R2
checks.note: The pattern was right: he lost rounds 1 and 2 and nearly finished Schmid late, but a round too late.

thomas-petersen-gabriel-lourenco.summary: Petersen took the debuting Lourenco down early and reached his back, but Lourenco escaped and turned the round: an illegal knee to the grounded Petersen that the referee missed, then a left hook and a right hand that floored him twice and knees and elbows against the fence; Petersen survived, and two judges scored it 10-8. Lourenco had emptied his tank, and Petersen dropped him with a left hook in the first minute of round 2 and nearly finished him; in round 3 he took him down, worked from half guard with elbows and punches, and the referee stopped it at 4:47, 13 seconds from what would likely have been a majority draw.
thomas-petersen-gabriel-lourenco.turning_point: The opening of round 2: Petersen's left hook that dropped an exhausted Lourenco.

checks.note: Lourenco was the one who tired: gassed by the end of round 1 and spent in round 3.
Takedowns in rounds 1 and 3; the finish came from top position.

karine-silva-gabriella-fernandes.summary: Most of the fight was clinch work on the fence, where the bigger Fernandes kept reversing position and kneeing the body; Silva took round 1 on Sherdog's cards by countering a takedown into top position at the horn. Fernandes swept Silva off her feet with a low kick in round 2 and won it, and Silva took round 3 with the busier boxing. Silva won 29-28 on all three cards and all three of Sherdog's; the outlets called it flat.

checks.claim: Silva wins the grappling exchanges over 15 minutes against a fighter held down by grapplers: decision
checks.note: Decision right, but Fernandes was the stronger in the clinch; Silva's one takedown came at the end of round 1 and she won round 3 standing.

murtazali-magomedov-jose-mauro-delano.summary: Delano won round 1 with leg kicks and volume until he slipped on a kick and Magomedov landed on top. Magomedov took him down twice in round 2 and landed a head kick, but Delano got up each time and finished the round strongly to the body, and he was the fresher man in round 3, buckling Magomedov with a leg kick. Magomedov's late takedown and an overhand left that dropped Delano in the closing seconds won him 29-28 on all three official cards; all three Sherdog scorers had Delano 29-28.
murtazali-magomedov-jose-mauro-delano.turning_point: The knockdown in the last seconds of round 3, which by MMA Mania's account swung the round.

austin-bashi-carlos-calderon.summary: Calderon, on four days' notice, came out aggressive and they traded wildly before Bashi drove through for a takedown. Bashi shed a guillotine, scrambled to the back and finished with a rear-naked choke at 1:07 of round 1.

andre-petroski-mantas-kondratavicius.summary: Kondratavicius hit Petroski hard every time he came in during round 1, stuffing his early shots, and won it on all three Sherdog cards despite Petroski's late takedown to side control. In round 2 Petroski took him down again, smothered him in half guard, moved to the back and mount and broke him with punches and elbows until the stoppage at 4:39, ending a three-fight skid.

Turman had his best spell in round 2 with the jab, right hands and a spinning backfist (one Sherdog scorer gave him the round) until Ko took him down again. In round 3 Ko took him down in the first 30 seconds, passed to mount, attacked a von Flue choke and an arm-triangle and punched him to the bell: 30-27 on all three cards.

jose-henrique-souza-jonny-parsons.summary: Parsons, back after more than three years out, threw low kicks and head kicks but could not get past the 6-foot-3 Souza's jab, and landed little. Souza built on the jab with straight lefts and hooks and flattened him with a right uppercut and left hook at 4:16 of round 1.

checks.claim: Override: Parsons's rust shows once the pace rises against Souza's jab and knees: KO/TKO, R2
checks.note: Parsons was out-ranged and barely landed; the knockout came a round early and off the jab, not the knees.
